proposals: PNGRB should publish a downloadable register of every crude, product and LPG pipeline, giving operator, route, length, design capacity and whether it runs as own-use or common carrier, so the network’s company-by-company shape does not rest on one uncorroborated study putting it at 55 lines and 19,599 km.

PPAC should publish annual throughput and utilisation for each crude-oil trunk pipeline, so an all-India crude-pipeline utilisation figure exists alongside the product and gas figures, rather than being inferred from refineries running at 102.9 per cent of nameplate capacity.

PNGRB should publish the routes, lengths and authorisation status of the nine LPG pipelines, roughly 3,470 km, on which it consulted in late 2024, so progress in extending a network that carries about 2.5 of 32 million tonnes of LPG demand can be tracked.

IHB, the Indian Oil–HPCL–BPCL joint venture, should publish the Kandla–Gorakhpur pipeline’s capacity by phase and its dated commissioning milestones, so the conflicting 3.75 and 8.5 million-tonne figures are resolved and repeated delays can be measured against a stated schedule.
